newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow foreign workers to extend service.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow foreign workers to extend service.

text.p: Taiwan will allow its 260,000 foreign workers on the island to extend their contracts from two to three years after repeated demands by their employers, labour officials said on Saturday.
"The chairman has decided to allow the workers to work one more year in Taiwan after their two-year contracts expire," a spokesman of the Labour Affairs Council said by telephone.
He said council chairman Hsu Chieh-kuei gave the green light during a council meeting on Friday, but employers must apply on behalf of their employees for the extension of the service.
He expected the new measure to be effective next week after cabinet approval.

Taiwan has permitted nationals from Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines and Thailand to work in Taiwan. There are at present some 260,000 such workers, with Thais accounting for more than 60 percent of the foreign work force.
Workers are allowed to work no more than two years and must return home after their contracts expire.
Employers have protested against the requirement, saying it affects work efficency because many foreign workers have to leave Taiwan after they are trained and have begun to master their work.
